title: Napier Beats Florida at the Horn
dek: Trapped, limping and off balance, Shabazz Napier missed — then caught DeAndre Daniels' blind tip-back at the free-throw line and beat the horn: UConn 65, No. 15 Florida 64.

setup.text: Nothing forced this game onto the calendar — no league, no tournament. UConn and Florida signed up for a home-and-home series, and the Huskies chose to bring the Gators to small, loud Gampel Pavilion on campus instead of the bigger XL Center in Hartford.

UConn arrived 7-0 and had moved up to No. 12 in the AP poll released that Monday. It was already a team living on the edge: its wins over Maryland, Boston College and Indiana had each been decided by one or two points. Florida, No. 15 at 6-1, had lost only at Wisconsin, and this was UConn's first game of the season against a ranked opponent.

The Gators started four seniors, led by top scorer Casey Prather, and had point guard Scottie Wilbekin back from a suspension. But freshman guard Kasey Hill was out with an ankle injury and swingman DeVon Walker was hobbled by a foot sprain. The schools had met only once, in the 1994 Sweet 16, a 69-60 Florida win in overtime.
Gampel was sold out — 10,167 — with Jim Calhoun and George Blaney among UConn's guests on press row and more than 20 NBA scouts in the building.

story.text: Napier hit a 3 on UConn's first possession, but Florida's frontcourt pushed the Huskies around and the Gators led 24-16 with 5:49 left in the half. UConn answered from beyond the arc and went to the locker room up 30-29.

Florida came back out strong. A Prather layup made it 48-41 with 12:49 to play — the first time all season UConn had trailed by seven. Out of an Ollie timeout, Niels Giffey hit a 3 to start a 10-0 run, and Napier's 3 with 10:17 left put UConn ahead 51-48.

The lead changed hands six times in the final six minutes. With 3:01 left Florida lost Wilbekin to a sprained ankle; he went to the locker room and did not return. Billy Donovan switched to a 1-3-1 zone, and with UConn big man Phillip Nolan fouled out and Tyler Olander playing with four fouls, 6-foot-9 center Patric Young scored Florida's next seven points.

sequence.text: Wilbekin, Florida's point guard, hurts his ankle and is taken to the locker room. He will not return.
Patric Young ties it with a jumper.
After an Amida Brimah free throw, Young tips in a miss to put Florida back in front.
Young scores again and adds the free throw. Florida leads by three.
UConn misses two 3s — Napier's, then Lasan Kromah's — and gets the offensive rebound both times.
Napier swishes a 3 and is fouled by Dorian Finney-Smith, landing on Finney-Smith's foot. He stays on the floor for about a minute, holding his left ankle.
Ollie calls timeout so Napier can stay in and shoot. He makes the free throw: a four-point play.
Michael Frazier II drives the lane and scores off a screen. Florida leads again and calls timeout.

Florida traps Napier about 30 feet from the basket. The ball is knocked loose, he gets it back and throws up a wild, off-balance shot that misses. DeAndre Daniels, off balance himself, slaps it blindly back out.
The ball finds Napier alone at the free-throw line; his defenders had crashed the glass. He said about nine-tenths of a second remained when he grabbed it. His jumper drops as the horn sounds.

quotes.text: Growing up, I wanted to be Superman. Everyone wants to be a hero.
Point nine. Point eight. I just tried to shoot the ball as quick as I can but still shoot it regular.
It kind of reminded me of Richard Hamilton.... It was just a tap back and then the fade away shot.
The guy who won the game for them was DeAndre Daniels

aftermath.text: Bedlam followed, and Napier — who said he is “kind of claustrophobic” when piled on — ran for the locker room. His left ankle, taped unusually tight before the game by trainer James Doran, showed no swelling afterward, he said.
UConn stretched its start to 9-0 before Stanford beat the Huskies 53-51 at the XL Center on Dec. 18.
Florida did not lose again for four months. The Gators won 30 straight, a school record, and entered the NCAA tournament as the No. 1 overall seed.

The rematch came on April 5, 2014, in the national semifinals at AT&T Stadium. Before 79,444, UConn beat Florida again, 63-53, ending the streak — and two nights later the Huskies won the national championship.

legacy.text: Florida finished 36-3, and two of the three losses were to UConn: this one, by a single point, and the Final Four rematch.
It was UConn's first win ever over Florida, and Ollie said the tap-back and fadeaway reminded him of Richard Hamilton, author of one of the famous shots in Huskies history.
